articles.body: The progressive political action committee Justice Democrats has appointed Rev. Hodari Williams as its new executive director. The change sets the organization up to hone a civil rights message ahead of the 2028 election cycle, Williams told POLITICO. His appointment, shared first with POLITICO, comes at a time when self-proclaimed progressives (and socialists) are flooding the scene. The PAC has had its most successful election cycle ever, helping seven candidates — including Donavan McKinney in Michigan, Melat Kiros in Colorado and Darializa Avila Chevalier in New York — defeat incumbents in the primaries. While those candidates are heavily favored to win on Election Day, the fates of three other Justice Democrats candidates, including Tennessee’s state Rep. Justin Pearson, remain less certain going into November. At one point, the group tried to get Williams to run for office. Though he declined, Williams said now is the right time to force change. “America and its present-day politicians, from my experience, have a high blood pressure of promises and anemia of political courage,” Williams said in an interview, using a common Kenyan political expression. “Right now, JD is producing candidates who have the political courage to deal with the crises that are existing in marginalized and disenfranchised communities, and I want to be a part of that.” Williams, 46, was born and raised in Lakewood, New Jersey. His parents were activists and community organizers who raised him on the legacy of the Civil Rights Movement. After graduating from Francis Marion University in Florence, South Carolina, with his bachelor’s degree, he joined the NAACP as a field organizer for voter rights and empowerment while pursuing his Master’s of Divinity at the Interdenominational Theological Center. In his time with the NAACP, Williams traveled across the Black Belt, where he said he witnessed poverty and inequity up close. “Civil rights traditionally has been something that people have tried to separate from progressivism … but these movements are inseparable,” said Williams. “What I witnessed in the South as a worker in voter rights and voter empowerment and education, and as a regional representative for the NAACP, was that the conditions that created inequity still existed and needed to be confronted and challenged.” His work took him to Kenya, where he served as a program coordinator with the Presbyterian Church USA. In Nairobi, he supported the Green Belt Movement’s work against deforestation and its mission to highlight environmental justice as a tool for economic empowerment and self-determination. Now, as some Black and brown voters express concerns of being tokenized by traditional Democratic candidates, Williams plans to bring his experience working in racial justice circles to his new role. “I have worked in communities that have borne the brunt of failed promises from the current Democratic leadership,” Williams said. “I have opened the doors of my congregations to politicians and have experienced the absence of those politicians after the elections.” He continued: “Black communities have become destinations for environmental hazards and data centers. Unemployment has risen. Black federal employees have been targeted. The list goes on. I’ve pastored these people. I've prayed with them. I've listened to them as they've shed tears. Now I've decided I want to move from triage work to really transformational work.” Some of that work will require challenging other Black leaders. “Unfortunately, many of our Black politicians have become victims of corporate capture, and their voices have been taken by entities like AIPAC,” said Williams, referring to the American Israel Public Affairs Committee. “They have not really been able to stand for the issues that are affecting the communities that that many of us are fighting for, and JD candidates are free from that, and they're free to take bold and significant action to move forward legislation.” But with the 2026 election cycle nearly over, the PAC is already brainstorming how to establish a strong progressive coalition for the 2028 presidential election. That will mean convincing the mainstream Democratic party that Justice Democrats have built a lasting coalition of the party’s base, said Williams. “We hope that the Democratic Party would see that we're developing a blueprint to show them how the base is being energized around the issues that are kitchen table issues that people want us to deal with,” said Williams. “It's not enough for us just to have a call to defeat a fascist president. We don't want a fascist president. We want him out, but we also want a vision of what America could look like when affordability, healthcare, civil rights, housing, and livable wages — all of those things are at the top of the political agenda,” he added. Williams succeeds current executive director and co-founder Alexandra Rojas, who will become president of Justice Democrats’ board and will support Williams as a senior adviser.
articles.headline: Justice Democrats announce new executive director

articles.body: Iowa Rep. Ashley Hinson took a swipe at the savings habits of millennials as she fielded a question Wednesday about Social Security during a Senate campaign debate. Hinson, the Republican candidate facing off against Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek, was asked about ensuring the solvency of Social Security when she raised the broader prospect of savings by millennials, the demographic consisting of people born from 1981-1996. She said the country needed to have a “serious conversation” about “how young people are saving money,” as part of the discussion about the future of Social Security. “We also need to be talking about millennials saving money,” she later added. “Millennials are the worst group of savers in the country right now and have the least amount of savings. So those are ways where I think we can help have a bigger conversation around saving in general, planning for retirement and making sure we're all able to experience a robust retirement.” Hinson faces a tough race in Iowa against Turek amid a difficult political environment for Republicans. Voters are overwhelmingly pessimistic about the state of the economy and their own personal finances, and they support Social Security while being concerned about the program’s future . Hinson said she would not support cutting benefits and suggested creating a bipartisan commission to present suggestions to Congress to save the program. When pushed on her statement that “all options should be on the table,” she turned her attention to young people. “I think my dad and I had this discussion when I was in sixth grade, looking at a ledger book and trying to figure out, 'Hey, how are we going to make sure you're set up for your life?'” she said. “So we need to be having a conversation simultaneously to all solutions on the table, to make sure that it can stay solvent, while we're also talking about, 'How do we get more young people to save?'” "She has never and will never cut Social Security," Hinson campaign spokesperson Billy Fuerst said in a statement. Turek, when asked about Social Security, said he supports removing the payroll tax cap. “The best way we can keep this solvent is by taking off the cap,” Turek said. “Let's make sure that billionaires and large corporations are paying their fair share. That will move the needle in a very serious way to keep Social Security solvent.” Hinson disagreed. “The only thing I'm hearing from him is that the only solution to everything is to raise taxes,” she said.
articles.headline: Iowa’s Ashley Hinson slams the savings habits of millennials

articles.body: MO’ MONEY: Republican gubernatorial candidate Bruce Blakeman has received dozens of contributions surpassing the legal limit in recent months. Blakeman has yet to refund roughly $360,000 to donors who have given to him above the cap, as POLITICO first reported on Monday . Gubernatorial candidates are allowed to raise $9,000 from individuals for each election — so $18,000 if they have both a primary and a general. Blakeman dodged a June election, so he’s required to give back any money he’s raised above $9,000. Many of the excess contributions came early in the election cycle. Knicks owner James Dolan, for example, gave $18,000 on Jan. 20, before it was known whether there would be a primary. But there have been at least 40 donations above the $9,000 limit that have come in since the Board of Elections certified the primary ballot on May 13, according to Blakeman’s disclosure reports. Many of those came well past the primary. An Eric Sternberg who used a Nassau County PO Box, for example, gave Blakeman $15,000 in the spring. A donor with the same name who used a nearby home address gave $18,000 on Aug. 19; three more $5,000 checks from those Eric Sternbergs were reported on Sept. 10. In addition to those 40 donations, there are several individuals who have gone over the limit by making multiple contributions. Former Republican Rep. Nan Hayworth, for example, gave $5,205.08 on May 22, then the same amount on July 31, bringing her total to $10,410.16 for the election cycle. The unusual figure appears to arise from another way the Blakeman campaign is going past the $9,000 cap. His donation page asks people to make a supplemental contribution to cover processing fees — so somebody giving $5,000 gets a request to give an additional $205.08. Attempting to donate $9,000 brings forth a suggested donation of $9,369.14. That exact amount has been given 22 times, including by Nassau resident — and one-time Trump administration official — Anthony Scaramucci. “Anyone who looks at campaign finance filings will see every campaign eating the cost for processing fees,” Democratic campaign finance lawyer Ben Kallos said. “I admire the creativity of trying to have donors eat those costs, but you can’t go over the limit.” POLITICO asked the Blakeman campaign about the refunds it owes on Monday. It replied on Tuesday without addressing the issue. “So many New Yorkers opened their wallets to support Bruce Blakeman that the state’s antiquated campaign finance system couldn’t keep up,” spokesperson Madison Spanodemos said. “The Board of Elections required the campaign to split its most recent finance report into multiple files since it included so much data, causing some contributions to appear multiple times.” The Public Campaign Finance Board said it’s not to blame. “Mr. Blakeman’s campaign is the only filer that experienced this issue,” Democratic co-director Brian Keegan said. “This is a user error, not a system error.” Spanodemos did not respond to questions about the large donations or what the committee’s actual war chest is. If every potential duplicate is removed from Blakeman's filing, his contribution total would fall by $292,000. That would lower his balance to a $114,000 deficit, even before accounting for the $360,000 in refunds he owes. A shift like that wouldn’t be unprecedented. Blakeman’s previous report, submitted on July 15, showed he had $4.7 million in the bank. An amended version submitted on July 22 changed his balance to $6.1 million. Yet another amendment on Aug. 13 said that his war chest in mid-July had actually been $4.3 million. Gov. Kathy Hochul has recently received a handful of contributions over the limit as well. But as has been the norm for gubernatorial candidates, her committee has returned surpluses: The New York State Council of Machinists, for example, gave $10,000 on Sept. 15 and got $1,000 back on Sept. 28. Hochul’s campaign has started to make Blakeman’s campaign finance foibles an issue in recent weeks. “It’s against the law,” state Democratic Committee Chair Jay Jacobs said of the Republican’s large contributions. “He’s desperate for money, and desperate people do desperate things. And I think to him, it’s more important he try to get elected than comply with the law.” — Bill Mahoney ONE WEEK AWAY: Mayor Zohran Mamdani ’s administration is pursuing a bold agenda to tame the city’s affordability crisis — making New York City a testing ground for progressives across the country. Join POLITICO’s New York Outlook: Affordability, Industry & The Economy in NYC on Oct. 14 for live conversations about the business and policy decisions being made today that will shape the city’s economic future. The lineup includes NYC Comptroller Mark Levine , New York City Economic Development Corp. CEO Anthony Shorris , New York City Council Speaker Julie Menin , Partnership for NYC CEO Steven Fulop , Citizens Budget Commission President Andrew Rein , Charles H. Revson Foundation President Maria Torres-Springer , and more. Register now to attend in person or watch the livestream . FROM CITY HALL MAMDANI’S OCT. 7 MESSAGE: Mamdani marked the third anniversary of Hamas’ Oct. 7, 2023 attack by condemning the “horrific war crimes” that took place in Israel that day — and then proceeded to blast the American ally for the military campaign it launched in response. “On that day, Hamas killed more than 1,100 Israelis and abducted 251 others. We grieve alongside our many friends and neighbors who still carry that unthinkable loss,” he said in a written statement this morning. He then pivoted: “The suffering did not begin nor end that day. It instead continued through the Israeli government’s devastating, ongoing genocide in Gaza, in which it has killed more than 74,000 Palestinians — including more than 21,000 children … Many New Yorkers are reckoning with this unbearable grief, and we mourn alongside them — all while knowing that our tax dollars fund these war crimes.” Mamdani’s missive — which he also posted on X , where it had garnered nearly 11 million views as of early this afternoon — was consistent with how he has for years messaged regarding the events on and after Oct. 7. What’s remarkable is that he did it as mayor on a somber day — the kind of occasion for which elected officials typically deploy restraint. Today marked his first time commemorating the anniversary as mayor of New York City, home to the largest Jewish community outside Israel, swaths of which believe Mamdani has fomented antisemitism by accusing the country of commiting a genocide in Gaza, a charge Israeli leaders vehemently deny. Backlash to the mayor’s statement was swift. “It is like turning September 11 into a day of mourning for al-Qaeda terrorists,” Danny Danon, Israel’s ambassador to the United Nations, wrote on X in response to Mamdani’s comments. “We will not let this happen. We will remember those who were murdered, and we will never forget who was behind this massacre.” Rep. Dan Goldman, a fellow Democrat, called it a “reprehensible statement.” “In the guise of ‘grieving’ with those mourning that day, Mayor Mamdani asserts as fact hotly disputed allegations that he knows full well will offend and further upset those same people he pretends to grieve with,” Goldman wrote on X . “On this day of all days, the Mayor of the city with the largest Jewish population outside of Israel embraces extreme activism instead of balanced leadership.” A spokesperson for Mamdani declined to respond to such criticisms. The mayor is scheduled to attend an Oct. 7 remembrance vigil this evening. Hochul commemorated the anniversary by ordering the Israeli flag be hoisted on top of the Capitol in Albany. She also ordered that flags be flown at half mast at all state government buildings across New York. “It’s hard to fathom that it has been three years since the October 7 Hamas massacre. Three years since the deadliest day for the Jewish people since the Holocaust,” the governor said in a statement. “The pain of that dark day has not faded. But neither has the strength, resilience and enduring hope of the Jewish people.” — Chris Sommerfeldt From the Capitol FEDERAL TAX CREDIT UNDER FIRE: New York’s legislative leaders are urging Hochul to reject a GOP-backed federal tax credit scholarship program, setting up a potential clash over the hot-button issue. The Treasury Department released a pair of rules for the initiative — which was included in President Trump’s sweeping 2025 tax-and-spending package — last week. The program would give donors to nonprofits that support educational expenses a dollar-for-dollar tax credit of up to $1,700 annually. Married taxpayers filing jointly could receive a credit of up to $3,400. In a statement Wednesday, state Senate Majority Leader Andrea Stewart-Cousins said the regulations would undercut the state’s ability to establish “meaningful guardrails,” leaving New York with little control over which schools and expenses qualify or how the funding is used. She also said it would allow the money to potentially flow to schools outside the state. “I am apprehensive about this federal proposal and have serious reservations about the potential impact it could have on public schools across New York State,” Stewart-Cousins said. “New York should not opt in to this program.” Assembly Speaker Carl Heastie also said Tuesday that his chamber will prioritize ensuring public schools are fully funded. “Public dollars should support public schools that serve all children and are accountable to the taxpayers who fund them,” Heastie said in a statement. “New York should opt out of the federal voucher program and continue investing in the public schools that educate the overwhelming majority of our children.” The city’s and state’s teachers unions, with which the Legislature is closely aligned, have also urged Hochul to reject the program . Spokespeople for the governor did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the opposition of legislative leaders. But Hochul has signaled support for the scholarship program. Ahead of the release of the regulations, her office said the credits could expand educational opportunities for public and private school students statewide “without diverting resources from public schools or state and local budgets.” The governor’s team also said public schools could benefit from the program. — Madina Touré FROM THE CAMPAIGN TRAIL TAKING THE STAGE: A debate is on the books in the battleground race between Democratic Rep. Tom Suozzi and his Republican challenger, former Assemblymember Mike LiPetri. The debate, hosted by News 12, will air on Oct. 20. The station said that’s the only Long Island congressional debate it’s hosting after Democratic Rep. Laura Gillen and Chris Gallant, Republican Rep. Nick LaLota’s Democratic challenger, declined News 12’s invite for their respective races. Republican Rep. Andrew Garbarino’s campaign did not respond to its invite, the station said. Suozzi defeated LiPetri by 4 points in 2024. National Republicans are pouring millions into the seat in the final stretch of the race with the hope of flipping it this year. — Madison Fernandez POLL POSITION : Hochul leads Republican foe Bruce Blakeman by 11 points in a Marist University survey released this morning. Hochul, seeking a second full term, draws 53% in the poll; Blakeman stands at 42%. Voters by a 55% to 42% margin plan to support the Democratic congressional candidate, the survey found. The poll of 1,361 likely voters was conducted from Oct. 1 to Oct. 4. It has a 3.6 percentage point margin of error. — Nick Reisman IN OTHER NEWS — GROCERY BRANDING: Branding for Mamdani’s signature city-run grocery stores will be handled by the same Brooklyn design firm behind trendy products like Graza olive oil and Yellowbird hot sauce. ( New York Magazine ) — GENDER-AFFIRMING CARE: New York City plans to spend nearly $9 million on local organizations providing gender-affirming care to minors, after two major hospital systems in the city struck deals with the Trump administration to stop providing such care. articles.body: Michigan Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers called for an end to the “tariff war” with Canada in a new campaign advertisement released Wednesday, another break from the Trump administration weeks before the midterm elections. Rogers’ ad comes as Republican campaign groups across the country have entered triage mode in an effort to salvage GOP control in an unfavorable political environment. “Here in Michigan, we know that Canada is not our enemy. We need to end this tariff war now,” Rogers said in the advertisement , which is part of a coordinated spend between his campaign at the National Republican Senatorial Committee. He added, “as Michigan’s senator, I’ll bring both parties together to lower your prices.” Each year, Michigan does roughly $80 billion in trade with Canada, according to the Michigan Chamber of Commerce. The new video comes weeks after he put out another advertisement breaking with President Donald Trump, publicly calling for the war with Iran to end “quickly.” In both commercials, Rogers said that prices are too high and neither mentioned the president by name. The latest ad is a shift from his previous positioning on trade with Canada. Last month, Rogers said that some of the tariffs imposed on Canadian goods are needed, as the state’s manufacturing sector has been gutted by cheap foreign imports in the past. “President Trump is right to put America first — and tariffs are necessary, but are not a one-size-fits-all solution,” Rogers previously said in a press release . But, he also said he has the pull to end the trade war threatening Michigan. During a press conference in the Oval Office on Wednesday, Trump downplayed the suggestion that Rogers was breaking with him. "I viewed him as saying that he thinks Canada should make a deal," Trump said. "Canada has been ripping off our country for many, many years." Rogers’ and Democratic nominee Abdul El-Sayed’s campaigns did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
articles.headline: Michigan’s Mike Rogers says trade war with Canada needs to end

articles.body: National Republicans have spent months trying to rescue Ken Paxton. He’s complicating that effort. Tensions are brewing with some Republicans after POLITICO published Paxton’s closed-door comments that “D.C.” Republicans were largely controlling his race . “He is welcome to raise his own money and say whatever he wants,” said one Republican involved in the Paxton rescue effort, who like others in this article was granted anonymity to speak candidly. “In fact, if he did that, he’d probably be winning right now and we wouldn’t need to spend all this money.” "This just seems like Paxton preparing to blame others for what might be one of the most embarrassing defeats in modern political history," said Carlos Curbelo, a former Florida GOP representative. Senate Republicans and top operatives didn’t want to be in this position in the first place. Many had warned that the Trump effort to unseat Sen. John Cornyn and back Paxton in the primary would cost Republicans hundreds of millions to drag Paxton across the finish line in the general election. Cornyn and Senate GOP groups spent millions of dollars on ads during the primary attacking Paxton over his series of scandals and warning he was a flawed candidate. Since then, the usual crowd of never-Paxton types has expanded into a wider circle of frustrated Republicans who are irked by the effort it’s taking to boost the scandal-plagued Senate candidate. And Paxton saying he doesn’t control his campaign messaging — alongside his remarks that President Donald Trump’s midterm convention hurt him politically — isn’t helping. Paxton also complained about the drag of the Iran war and high prices on his campaign in another closed-door recording that Axios published Wednesday . “Beggars can’t be choosers. He can try to raise federal money at a level that is necessary to save his candidacy at this point but his arms don’t reach that high,” said a Texas-based GOP consultant who’s closely monitoring multiple races. “As usual, he communicates something that is unhelpful, that is undisciplined, that is politically self-harmful and like most things, lacks any gratitude whatsoever.” The top Senate GOP super PAC, Trump’s aligned MAGA Inc. operation and other Republicans are pumping more than $200 million into the race to salvage Paxton’s campaign against Democrat James Talarico. Trump allies say they have worked hard to shore up Paxton, suggesting they’ve pushed donations toward the campaign and the larger GOP super PAC effort to avoid disaster in the Lone Star State. Trump plans to travel to Texas for the second time Wednesday to boost Paxton. Paxton allies have brushed off his latest closed-door comments, saying he was referring to GOP super PACs he’s not allowed to coordinate with as a candidate. The Paxton campaign did not respond to a request for comment, though campaign adviser Nick Maddux said in response to POLITICO’s initial report of the audio that “AG Paxton is thankful for the support and knows how important Texas is to keeping the majority, which is why he’s on the ground every day.” But another Republican, a Trump ally working on the fundraising effort, said the national intervention isn’t overstepping. That person said the messaging guidance from the national GOP is standard for major Senate races and that Paxton “needs the help.” One national GOP operative involved in the Texas Senate race noted that the attorney general's lackluster fundraising early on left him vulnerable to Talarico’s attacks throughout the summer — especially over Paxton’s series of “self-inflicted” scandals, which have made him “toxic” with key voting blocs in the deep red state. “We warned them about this,” the GOP operative said. The Texas Senate race has sucked up oxygen, despite Trump winning the state in 2024 by double digits. And, the Senate map has kept expanding as Democrats have made gains in other typically red states, forcing Republicans to make critical decisions about where to allocate resources. Senate Majority Leader John Thune and Republicans have said there are dedicated donors who are backing their effort to help Paxton, as they also try to shore up red seats across the map. Paxton, in the September meeting with donors, acknowledged Washington’s influence. “I’ve never been in a race where I felt less control over the campaign … it’s all coming — you know — from D.C.,” Paxton told donors during a small fundraising event last month, according to the audio. Top GOP officials have tried to downplay Paxton’s comments. The White House referred POLITICO to the RNC when asked for comment. The RNC argued Paxton, in the audio, was referring to the super PACs he can’t coordinate with as a candidate. "This is fake news nonsense mixed with lazy reporting demonstrating a clear ignorance about how super PACs work. President Trump has called Ken Paxton the single greatest attorney general in history and has been clear he will do whatever it takes to make him the next senator from Texas,” RNC spokesperson Zach Kraft said in a statement. Trump, when speaking to reporters at the White House on Tuesday, said he hadn’t seen Paxton’s latest comments. He added that his midterm travel blitz has helped Paxton and other Republican candidates. “Ken’s doing much better now that I — everybody is — since starting three, four days ago, since starting the rallies. It’s brought a whole new awareness to how great the Republicans are doing, how great the economy is doing,” Trump said, touting investments and manufacturing. The president last week traveled to Texas and told the crowd that Paxton is a “pain in the ass sometimes” and later acknowledged he’s “a little controversial." But, he also warned the Texas crowd that Talarico would be “such a horror to your state,” adding, “we need the votes and I'm here for that, and I think we're going to win.” Vance also traveled to Texas, where he called Paxton an “amazing attorney general and your next senator.” Still, other Republicans have simply grown resigned to the state of the race, with Paxton needing all the aid he can get. “There is only so much we can do,” one senior Senate GOP aide said. “And I feel like we’re doing a lot.” The Paxton campaign told POLITICO it raised $18 million in the third quarter across the campaign and his joint fundraising committees. That’s roughly double his second-quarter total, though the campaign did not provide its cash-on-hand numbers, and Talarico has yet to release his fundraising haul. Paxton also announced a $20 million ad buy last week — a significant single media investment in the race. But he’s had to rely heavily on Trump, MAGA Inc. and the top Senate GOP super PAC to bail him out. Republicans have largely leaned on the Senate Leadership Fund, rather than the Trump-aligned MAGA Inc. super PAC, to keep Paxton afloat. SLF is spending a Texas record-breaking $131 million sum through Oct. 12 and has pledged to continue to spend more through the final weeks of the election. MAGA Inc. is increasing some spending for Paxton and is expected to hit near $45 million by Oct. 12. If Paxton were to lose, Trump’s reaction and whether he chooses to distance himself from the rescue effort will be driven by media coverage, said a former Trump fundraiser. “If the media coverage related to election night and the autopsy a couple days afterwards is brutal towards Trump, like, horrible economy, inflation's not that much better than the last year of Joe Biden's ... he will lash out,” the person said. “But if the narrative is, it’s a midterm presidential, this is what normally happens … he'll move on as fast as he can and never talk about Ken Paxton again. It just depends what the coverage looks like post the November election.” Myah Ward contributed to this report.
articles.headline: Paxton’s latest audio leak is making things tough for national Republicans

articles.body: The 2026 House map continues to move further onto GOP terrain. But while Democrats are dreaming big, the GOP insists they can hold the majority. Score talked to the DCCC's Deputy Executive Director Will Van Nuys and the NRCC's Communications Director Will Kiley. The two operatives chose four under-the-radar races where they’re feeling good about their underdog candidates pulling off an upset. If these races flip, they know they’re having a good night. “We're not saying that this won't be a tough fight to the end, but we know we feel very good about where we stand,” Kiley said. “Our job is to make sure that we raise as much as we can to expand this battlefield as far as we can,” Van Nuys said. DEMOCRATS’ FOUR 'SLEEPER' SEATS CO-05 (Trump +9.1) Rep. Jeff Crank won this seat by 14 points in 2024 in his third bid for Congress. But Colorado Springs is “trending Democrats’ way” with fast growth of younger and Hispanic populations. That shift, along with Trump’s unpopularity, has Democrats hoping for a flip, Van Nuys says. IA-02 (Trump +10) Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson’s run for Senate has left this northeastern Iowa seat open for the taking, Van Nuys argues. Frustrations with beef imports, rising gas prices and the popularity of Democratic gubernatorial candidate Rob Sand have Democrats hoping state Rep. Lindsay James can turn this seat blue. KY-06 (Trump +15) Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear is making it his personal mission to elect his former adviser and federal prosecutor Zach Dembo and flip Senate nominee Rep. Andy Barr’s Lexington-based seat. Dembo released an internal poll in late September showing him with a 5-point lead. WI-01 (Trump +4.5) Van Nuys says emergency room nurse Mitchell Berman is a “perfect contrast” in the blue-collar district to Republican Rep. Bryan Steil, an attorney and former plastics manufacturing executive. FOUR DISTRICTS WHERE THE GOP THINKS IT CAN SURPRISE NM-02 (Trump +1.8) Former Republican Rep. Yvette Herrell ran four cycles in a row. Now the GOP is betting on a fresh face: Greg Cunningham, a tattooed, motorcycle-driving Marine vet and ex-cop who’s running ads highlighting his Hispanic heritage in the Latino-heavy district. Republicans are spending big on the race. Kiley called Cunningham a “badass.” “Greg is a candidate who can continue to capture those voters and keep them coming our way,” he said. NY-03 (Trump +4.3) Republican former state Assemblymember Mike LiPetri came within 4 points of defeating Rep. Tom Suozzi (D-N.Y.) in 2024, and Republican Nassau County Executive Bruce Blakeman coasted to reelection last fall. Now Blakeman is running for governor, and Kiley says the statewide campaign can push LiPetri over the top in a rematch. The MAGA Inc.-affiliated No Going Back PAC has dropped a whopping $6 million into the district, with $2 million more from NRCC, though the CLF trimmed its own ad buy there Tuesday. “Last cycle, LiPetri came incredibly close with minimal to no outside investment,” Kiley said. “Now he has the investment and institutional support to get the job done.” AZ-01 (Trump +3.1) The DCCC’s preferred candidate lost to former Democratic state Rep. Amish Shah in the primary in this Phoenix and Scottsdale-area seat, and Kiley says that’s opened the door for the GOP to hold the seat. “The DCCC is lying if they said that Amish is the candidate they wanted,” Kiley said. Republicans nominated former Arizona Cardinals kicker and NFL commentator Jay Feely, and Kiley says Feely’s unique resume will boost him over the edge. Both parties are spending huge sums, with more than $31 million combined earmarked for the race. NV-03 (Trump +0.7) Republican Marty O’Donnell was the composer for the music in the popular video game Halo. He’s using that success to pour $3 million into his bid to flip this Las Vegas-area seat held by Democratic Rep. Susie Lee. The personal investments, along with outside GOP spending , eliminate a cash advantage past Democrats enjoyed in the district, Kiley said. “The resources are coming in to flip this seat because the GOP ecosystem can see how big of an opportunity it is,” he said. articles.body: Leaders of the U.S. Hispanic Business Council knew it would be hard to get Ken Paxton to show up to their Senate town hall event. So, they turned to an unexpected ally: Sen. Ted Cruz. Javier Palomarez, the council’s president and CEO, needed help since his own background – as both a Democrat and longtime ally of Paxton’s rival in the primary, Sen. John Cornyn – wouldn’t appeal to the Texas attorney general. Cruz, however, was eager to step in. Soon, Palomarez was discussing logistics for the town hall with Paxton’s team; Paxton joined the event last week. “We needed to find common ground and people that he trusted, that I trusted … and that clearly was Ted Cruz,” Palomarez said. “I don't agree with Ted on a litany of shit, but at the end of the day, the guy's always been a good partner to me and to the small business community.” Cruz’s involvement hints at the significant behind-the-scenes role he is playing in this year’s high-stakes Texas Senate race — part-time adviser, part-time bundler, full-time believer that Paxton will pull out a win and keep Cruz from representing Texas alongside a Democrat. Paxton’s inner circle is dotted with longtime Cruz allies, and Cruz’s aid could further cement his position as a Texas kingmaker in retiring GOP Sen. John Cornyn’s absence, earn new allies and boost his national profile ahead of a potential 2028 presidential bid . But if Paxton fails, it could be a black eye for Cruz. “It is absolutely critical that Texas stay red, that Republicans keep a majority in the U.S. Senate and the House, and that we elect Ken Paxton instead of James Talarico,” Cruz said in an interview. “And so I am all in.” Paxton’s campaign declined to comment for this story. For decades, Cornyn has been the gatekeeper to Texas’ GOP donor class. But his loss has put Cruz even more at the center of Texas' deep-pocketed donor community, letting him flex muscles first developed during his 2016 presidential run as Paxton tries to hold off Talarico and his fundraising machine. Paxton raised $18 million in the last quarter, some of those donations coming from first-time donors introduced to him by Cruz. “Ted doesn't go through a meeting in Texas where he's not telling donors they’ve got to get on board,” said one person close to both Cruz and Paxton, granted anonymity to discuss private conversations. Cruz has regularly campaigned alongside Paxton and frequently jabs Talarico on his popular podcast . His super PAC has gone on air with anti-Talarico advertising. And in addition to greasing the rails with his big-money donors in the Lone Star State, he’s acting as an informal adviser, regularly speaking withPaxton, according to two people familiar with their conversations.The political orbits of Cruz and Paxton have significant overlap. Axiom Strategies — the GOP firm run by Jeff Roe, who led Cruz’s 2016 presidential campaign — has long worked with both men. Nick Maddux, senior adviser to the Paxton campaign, was a key staffer in Cruz’s 2018 and 2024 reelection efforts. Sam Cooper, a longtime Cruz adviser, is now a senior strategist for the pro-Paxton Lone Star Liberty PAC. Cruz stayed neutral during the messy primary between Cornyn and Paxton. He came off the sidelines after the runoff. “Ted was one of the first ones that understood that, hey, this guy just got hit with $200 million of negative advertising. He's running against an opponent who's going to be well-funded,” said Cooper. “He's going to need some help.” Within a week of Paxton’s primary runoff victory in May, Cruz emceed a Washington fundraiser for Paxton, urging attendees to come together and support the Republican nominee. Days later, Cruz joined Paxton for a Texas fly-around, stopping in Dallas, Houston and Midland all in one day, to meet with donors. Cruz said they secured $3 million in donations on that day. Cruz has presented himself as an emissary between more traditional GOP donors and Paxton’s hardline MAGA world. “The case I've been making to donors who previously supported John Cornyn is, at this point, it's a binary choice, and I think the choice is very clear,” Cruz said, noting he’s had “hundreds of conversations” with donors. “Many, if not most, of the longtime Paxton donors are also supporters of mine, but many, if not most, of the longtime Cornyn donors are supporters of mine, as well. And so I do think I'm able to bridge those two worlds.” But Cruz’s involvement also carries some risk. Paxton is trailing in most recent polls, and Democrats are increasingly hopeful this is the cycle they finally flip a Texas Senate seat. If Paxton goes down, he could stifle Cruz’s momentum ahead of 2028, when other Republican hopefuls may attempt to lay the blame at Cruz’s feet. "This is smart on Ted’s part,” said one longtime Texas Republican strategist not affiliated with either man, granted anonymity to speak openly. “It cements him with Paxton supporters as being the guy who stood up for him, and it allows him to expand his reach and have a greater claim on having a unified Texas behind him if he makes a run in 2028." If Paxton loses, “he put his best foot forward, and it's going to be Paxton's fault that he lost, not Ted Cruz's,” the person said. Cruz’s super PAC, Truth and Courage, was one of the first to go up backing Paxton, reserving over $2 million on air with an anti-Talarico ad , according to data from tracking firm AdImpact — though that spend has since been swamped by major buys from the Senate Leadership Fund’s PAC and other pro-Republican groups. Cruz has hosted or participated in several fundraisers for Paxton, both in person and on Zoom. One of them — a fundraiser hosted by Cruz’s PAC on the sidelines of the Republican midterm convention, a confab Paxton later said “dropped our numbers” — featured dozens of donors crammed into an apartment in a glitzy uptown Dallas high-rise, in such close quarters that some of Paxton’s staffers were relegated to work on the balcony. “It was incredibly well attended,” recalled Rep. Randy Fine (R-Florida), who spoke at the fundraiser. “You couldn’t move.”

Fue en ese momento cuando se conoció la muerte de Maricarmen Abascal. La noticia fue difundida por el Sindicato de Inquilinas de Madrid a través de un breve texto en sus redes sociales. Solo 45 minutos después, la cuenta de Vox en X, antes Twitter, escribió que la habían asesinado: “Han matado a Maricarmen. Sin ningún escrúpulo han utilizado el sufrimiento de una persona mayor para montar una campaña que ocultase la responsabilidad del Gobierno en el desastre de la vivienda”. El mensaje ya ha sido visto por más de dos millones de usuarios. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-08/el-bulo-ultra-del-asesinato-de-maricarmen-procede-una-autopsia-zurdos-de-mierda-el-psoe-hara-todo-para-ganar-las-elecciones.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>La fulminante <a href="https://elpais.com/internacional/2026-10-07/los-medios-internacionales-se-hacen-eco-de-la-muerte-de-maricarmen.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/internacional/2026-10-07/los-medios-internacionales-se-hacen-eco-de-la-muerte-de-maricarmen.html">noticia de la muerte de Maricarmen Abascal</a> se acogió primero como broma de mal gusto por parte de muchos en Sol, y cuando empezó a coger vuelo y se iluminaron los móviles dentro y fuera de las tiendas de campaña, llegó la consternación seguida de la furia. Mientras tanto, tal y como los pájaros anticipan las catástrofes climáticas, ya estaba la policía tomando posiciones alertada de lo que podía significar esta muerte. articles.body: <p>La muerte de Maricarmen <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-08/el-aviso-de-los-acampados-en-sol-en-la-madrugada-no-habra-mas-maricarmenes.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-08/el-aviso-de-los-acampados-en-sol-en-la-madrugada-no-habra-mas-maricarmenes.html">ha causado una conmoción en el ya candente debate por la vivienda</a>, que ha llevado a la instalación de acampadas en distintas ciudades del país. articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/AJDW53HVSBDOBNP45L5RKK5T4I.jpg?auth=1578af4f1d935842dd14ef2c50830989df30463a570829659a197f7f4d197363" width="2362" height="1574" alt="Xosé Manuel Beiras, durante una asamblea en Santiago de Compostela en 2016."></img><p><a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/xose-manuel-beiras/" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/xose-manuel-beiras/">Xosé Manuel Beiras</a> ha fallecido a los 90 años en la madrugada de este jueves después de una intensa vida política. Némesis de los populares Manuel Fraga y Alberto Núñez Feijóo, el histórico dirigente del nacionalismo gallego lideró el BNG durante más de dos décadas y, tras abandonarlo, impulsó una alianza entre el soberanismo gallego y la izquierda federal que acabó siendo un referente para los nuevos partidos que nacieron en la España inflamada de la Gran Recesión. En los últimos tiempos, Beiras había vuelto a mostrar su apoyo al <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-galicia/2024-02-07/el-nacionalismo-gallego-afronta-su-examen-decisivo-en-su-mejor-momento.html" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-galicia/2024-02-07/el-nacionalismo-gallego-afronta-su-examen-decisivo-en-su-mejor-momento.html">Bloque que ahora lidera Ana Pontón</a>. “Deja una huella en varias generaciones de gallegos y gallegas, entre las que me incluyo”, ha escrito Pontón en las redes sociales sobre quien considera un “referente de coraje, compromiso y amor por Galicia”. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-08/muere-a-los-90-anos-xose-manuel-beiras-historico-dirigente-del-nacionalismo-gallego.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

Llevan residiendo allí desde que se hipotecaron con Bankia hace más de 20 años. Sin embargo, según describen, la hipoteca pasó a ser propiedad de CaixaBank y no han conseguido llegar a un acuerdo sobre los pagos de las cuotas, que aseguran que abonaban. Finalmente, les llegó la notificación de que tenían que abandonar la vivienda hace dos meses, el 31 de julio.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-08/el-goteo-incesante-de-desalojos-no-da-tregua-a-los-acampados-en-sol-despertad-hay-un-desahucio-cerca-necesitamos-gente.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/6RNEQN6KA5AZHJ5OLTYZBRCBSQ.jpg?auth=ab46d733691f9397eb63175905cfd61dacd4de255fd8e6d1fc4c718caefdf6ca" width="1146" height="650" alt="Un migrante camina de vuelta a Marruecos, en la frontera de El Tarajal, para abandonar la ciudad de Ceuta, este lunes."></img><p>Los <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/el-desalojo-de-la-playa-de-el-trampolin-dispara-los-regresos-voluntarios-en-ceuta-900-retornos-en-un-dia.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/el-desalojo-de-la-playa-de-el-trampolin-dispara-los-regresos-voluntarios-en-ceuta-900-retornos-en-un-dia.html">desalojos efectuados por la Policía Nacional</a> en las playas de Benítez y de El Trampolín, en Ceuta, han desembocado en cientos y cientos de “retornos voluntarios” a Marruecos, acelerando el ritmo de salidas exponencialmente. Más de 2.500 migrantes han abandonado la ciudad autónoma en una semana, durante y después de los operativos policiales para desmantelar los asentamientos, según cifras actualizadas por La Moncloa, a las que ha accedido EL PAÍS. Está previsto que este jueves el ministro Ángel Víctor Torres, al frente del mando único desde el 25 de agosto, desgrane los datos en una comparecencia de prensa en la Delegación de Gobierno tras la reunión semanal del Comité de Situación. En total, desde el 10 de agosto han regresado a Marruecos unas 11.000 personas <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-07/el-gobierno-de-ceuta-lleva-ante-notario-mas-mensajes-con-moncloa-buenas-tardes-diego-director-de-gabinete-de-sanchez-alguna-noticia.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-07/el-gobierno-de-ceuta-lleva-ante-notario-mas-mensajes-con-moncloa-buenas-tardes-diego-director-de-gabinete-de-sanchez-alguna-noticia.html">que llegaron en el cruce masivo</a> (entre las que se incluye también las devoluciones por infracción, que no superan las 500). </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-08/el-gobierno-registra-11000-retornos-de-migrantes-de-ceuta-a-marruecos-en-dos-meses.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
articles.headline: El Gobierno registra 11.000 retornos de migrantes de Ceuta a Marruecos en dos meses

articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/CPVCX6TO5FGC5DAFTQDBPNZQ34.jpg?auth=fb9602155603fdf7bec47d833e2823d8d58f37ddb7c19c94204992388cd3ad40" width="6000" height="4000" alt="El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, comparece en rueda de prensa tras la reunión del Consejo de Ministros, este martes en el Palacio de La Moncloa."></img><p>Pedro Sánchez fue muy claro este martes, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-05/sanchez-arenga-a-sus-ministros-salimos-a-ganar-y-vamos-a-ganar.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-05/sanchez-arenga-a-sus-ministros-salimos-a-ganar-y-vamos-a-ganar.html">tras un Consejo de Ministros</a> que aprobó dos decretos de emergencia sobre vivienda: “El Gobierno va a continuar gobernando”. El Ejecutivo no está en funciones hasta que se vote, tiene plenitud de facultades, y además tiene la ventaja de que lo que apruebe<a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-05/el-consejo-de-ministros-aprobara-manana-los-decretos-de-vivienda-para-que-los-vote-la-diputacion-permanente.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-05/el-consejo-de-ministros-aprobara-manana-los-decretos-de-vivienda-para-que-los-vote-la-diputacion-permanente.html"> se convalida en la Diputación Permanente</a>, un órgano donde Junts no es imprescindible, basta con lograr el apoyo del PNV además del de los socios de izquierdas de la coalición PSOE-Sumar (ERC, Bildu y Podemos). Por eso, el Ejecutivo está estudiando diversas posibilidades para explotar hasta el último momento la gran ventaja de controlar el Boletín Oficial del Estado, esto es, poder aprobar medidas sociales hasta el último día. Los ministerios y La Moncloa trabajan en distintas ideas, que irán desplegándose a lo largo de las semanas, según fuentes del Ejecutivo.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-08/el-gobierno-estirara-al-maximo-el-consejo-de-ministros-hasta-las-elecciones-con-decretos-sociales.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>“Decían que habían entrado 800 migrantes por Benzú, pero al hacer una inspección por el monte solo se veían unas cabras”, cuenta un agente de Ceuta. El 23 de septiembre, día en el que se celebraban las elecciones parlamentarias en Marruecos, la ciudad volvía a estar en vilo ante el temor de que repitiera una entrada masiva como la de los 30 y 31 de julio, en la que unas 80.000 personas accedieron a la ciudad en cuestión de horas. Un falso aviso de entrada, de entre 200 y 800 personas, según los mensajes, corrió por los chats y canales de Whatsapp de vecinos y puso en alerta a los medios. Varias fuentes policiales negaron que hubiera llegado a cruzar alguna persona, pero la noticia salió en varias televisiones. Hubo un intento de entrada de algo más de un centenar de migrantes, que se frenó desde Marruecos, pero esta información ni corrió, ni caló tan rápido como la inicial. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-08/los-100-bulos-de-ceuta-migrantes-que-llegan-por-tuneles-agua-en-mal-estado-y-falsas-entradas-masivas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>La estrategia de la primera semana de precampaña de Alberto Núñez Feijóo hacia las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre no la ha decidido el líder del PP, sino la presidenta de la Comunidad de Madrid, lsabel Díaz Ayuso. Suya es la idea de <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-07/no-votes-por-correo-la-campana-del-pp-de-ayuso-en-instagram-entre-risas-y-aplausos-de-diputados.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-07/no-votes-por-correo-la-campana-del-pp-de-ayuso-en-instagram-entre-risas-y-aplausos-de-diputados.html">cuestionar el sistema electoral español sembrando sospechas sobre la posibilidad de que el voto por correo sea manipulado,</a> un marco en el que acabó entrando este miércoles, dos días después de que lo dijera Ayuso, el líder del PP, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-07/feijoo-abona-a-las-dudas-del-pp-sobre-el-voto-por-correo-y-pedira-mas-controles-a-la-junta-electoral.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-07/feijoo-abona-a-las-dudas-del-pp-sobre-el-voto-por-correo-y-pedira-mas-controles-a-la-junta-electoral.html">al anunciar que pedirá “medidas adicionales” de seguridad a la Junta Electoral Central.</a> Feijóo no quería poner el foco en este tema, sino en la corrupción del PSOE y en la crisis de Ceuta, donde viajó este miércoles como muestra de que la ciudad autónoma será una de las prioridades de su campaña. Pero Ayuso terminó arrastrando a Feijóo a “pegarse un tiro en el pie” al sembrar dudas sobre el sistema electoral, según opinan fuentes de los sectores más moderados del PP, aunque otros dirigentes creen que este tipo de polémicas ayudan a movilizar al electorado de la derecha. Feijóo prepara una campaña al choque y de tono agresivo, como revela su decisión de aupar a los perfiles más duros a la primera línea. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-08/ayuso-arrastra-a-feijoo-al-laberinto-del-voto-por-correo.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: El vot per correu és un dret que recull la llei electoral, la LOREG . El poden exercir aquelles persones que estan inscrites al cens electoral . Depenent de la contesa electoral, poden votar uns ciutadans o uns altres. A les eleccions generals 2026 poden votar tots els ciutadans espanyols, visquin en territori espanyol o a l’estranger. Ho poden fer per correu o en ocasions en urnes que s’instal·len a ambaixades i consolats que exerceixen la funció de meses electorals. També et pot interessar Pedro Sánchez convoca eleccions generals el 29 de novembre després del no als decrets d’habitatge Jaume Planagumà Roger Torres i Liñán 2 minuts de lectura I com es compta aquest vot per correu i el vot exterior el dia de les eleccions? Segueixen procediments diferents. El vot per correu es barreja amb l’ordinari, però l’exterior no es compta fins dies després de la jornada electoral. Com es barreja el vot per correu amb l’ordinari? El vot per correspondència és certificat i es dirigeix al col·legi electoral que pertoca. El dia de les eleccions, abans que obrin els col·legis, el personal de Correus porta els sobres amb els vots a cada mesa . Allà es custodien durant la jornada. A les 20 h, hora del tancament, i després que hagi votat l’últim elector, es comprova que cada sobre inclogui la documentació que pertoca: un altre sobre amb la papereta i el certificat d’inscripció en el cens. Es comprova també que la persona estigui inscrita en aquella mesa i el sobre s’introdueix dins l’urna . És aleshores quan comença l’escrutini sense que hi hagi cap diferència entre els vots per correu i els dipositats presencialment. Què passa amb el vot exterior? El vot exterior segueix una altra via. Els ciutadans espanyols residents a l’estranger han d’estar inscrits en el cens que s’anomena CERA . Són els consolats i ambaixades els que actuen com a oficines del cens. Els electors poden votar directament en urnes que s’hi instal·len o fer-ho per correu a través dels mateixos consolats. A través d’ enviaments urgents i valises diplomàtiques (no poden ser aturades ni obertes) les ambaixades remeten els vots a les juntes electorals corresponents . Dies després de les eleccions es fa el que es coneix com a escrutini general , que és la comptabilització i revisió de les actes de les meses. És aquell dia que les juntes electorals es constitueixen a les 8 h com a meses i registren els vots dels espanyols residents a l’estranger, que s’afegeixen a la resta de resultats. El vot exterior s’hi suma en aquest moment, però es pot consultar de forma separada, com si d’una circumscripció més es tractés.
articles.headline: Com funciona el vot per correu a les eleccions generals 2026? I el vot exterior?

articles.body: El Gran Recapte ja té data per al 2026: serà el 13 i el 14 de novembre . En un context en què omplir el cistell d’anar a comprar costa més d’un 30 % més que fa cinc anys, l’edició d’enguany es dedica, per primera vegada, a un col·lectiu concret: les noves pobreses . Segons dades del Banc d’Aliments, a Catalunya hi ha 170.000 persones que necessiten el seu suport cada mes . També et pot interessar Quin és el supermercat més car i més barat de Barcelona? I de Catalunya? Olga Borràs Boada 3 minuts de lectura Les noves pobreses Des del Banc dels Aliments remarquen que en els darrers anys s’ha encarit el menjar, però també altres despeses essencials per al dia a dia . En concret, entre el 2020 i el 2025 el cost de la vida va augmentar un 21 % en general i un 32 % en el cas dels aliments. L’oli d’oliva, per exemple, es va apujar un 70 %; els ous, un 49 %, i la llet, un 44 %. També es van encarir per damunt del 30 % productes com els cereals i derivats, la fruita fresca i les patates. La situació, alerten, “té un impacte especial en les llars amb menys marge econòmic “, perquè les despeses bàsiques tenen més pes en la seva economia. Tenir feina “ja no garanteix en tots els casos que una família pugui pagar el pis, la llum, i els subministraments bàsics i tenir prou marge per comprar aliments en condicions”, com tampoc no ho garanteix cobrar una pensió de jubilació. També et pot interessar Els ingressos dels empresaris augmenten tres cops més que els dels assalariats, segons la UGT Helena Molist Sancho 1 minut de lectura Calen 17.000 voluntaris Aquesta és la 18a edició de la recollida solidària d’aliments i hi participaran 2.100 establiments col·laboradors arreu de Catalunya, com cadenes d’alimentació, mercats municipals i comerços de proximitat, a més de prop de 600 entitats i 400 empreses. Per poder tirar-ho endavant, però, calen encara 17.000 persones voluntàries , una figura que el Banc dels Aliments considera fonamental. Asseguren que als punts de recollida on hi ha persones voluntàries es multipliquen les donacions . Per això, tenint en compte les dades, “és bàsic sumar el màxim nombre de persones voluntàries”. Si hi vols participar, les inscripcions estaran obertes a partir d’aquest dijous i també és possible fer els primers donatius. També et pot interessar El Banc dels Aliments demana donacions també a l’agost: “La necessitat d’aliments no fa vacances” Jaume Planagumà Merche Artacho Vega 2 minuts de lectura El 2025 es van recaptar 5,2 milions d’euros en aliments , sumant el valor del menjar que es va recollir i les donacions econòmiques. Tot plegat, va permetre distribuir, 20.800 tones de menjar , que es van repartir entre més de 500 entitats socials. Es va recollir, entre d’altres, oli, llet i conserves, a més d’aliments d’alt valor nutritiu com peix, carn i ous.

articles.body: L’endemà d’haver mort , la Maricarmen , el símbol de la lluita per l’habitatge, ja té un mural a Barcelona. El signa l’artista urbà TVBoy i l’ha pintat aquest dijous al matí a la paret d’un edifici situat a la confluència dels carrers de Rec Comtal i les Basses de Sant Pere, al barri de Sant Pere, Santa Caterina i la Ribera. “Maricarmen per sempre” , ha escrit l’artista a la part superior del dibuix, en què es pot veure la Maricarmen convertida en un àngel i amb les claus del pis del qual va ser desnonada a la mà. L’homenatge de TVBoy a aquesta veïna de 87 anys desnonada del seu pis de Madrid després de 70 anys de viure-hi, se suma a les múltiples mostres d’afecte i condol que s’han produït durant les últimes hores, en conèixer-se la seva mort. El cas de la Maricarmen —que va haver de ser hospitalitzada just després de ser expulsada de casa seva— ha generat un terratrèmol social i polític, amb manifestacions multitudinàries , acampades , l’ avançament d’eleccions i la convocatòria d’una vaga general . També et pot interessar Mor la Maricarmen, la dona desnonada de Madrid convertida en un símbol de la crisi de l’habitatge Jessica Moreno Cusac 2 minuts de lectura

articles.body: La pluja excepcional d’aquests darrers dies podria tenir encara un darrer capítol aquest dijous. Amb el pas d’un potent embossament d’aire fred en altura es podran reactivar les tempestes en algunes comarques, sobretot de la costa i el nord-est . També et pot interessar Aiguats excepcionals de més de 200 litres: Barcelona viu un episodi de pluja històrica Ariadna Corominas del Hoyo Manel Cascante Torrella 3 minuts de lectura El rebuf de dijous vespre nit, the last dance d’aquest episodi El pas d’un potent solc amb aire fred en altura reactivarà les tempestes aquest dijous , però només en algunes comarques. L’entrada de la tramuntana i el mestral comportaran un canvi radical d’escenari respecte de la pluja que hem tingut durant la setmana. Amb l’entrada d’aquests vents, es farà neteja de núvols a bona part del territori, però una petita porció, arrecerada del vent, encara pot rebre algun patac d’aigua important. També et pot interessar Què és el fenomen meteorològic del rebuf? Manel Cascante Torrella 3 minuts de lectura És el que es coneix com a rebuf i que comporta que en el tram de costa i prelitoral comprès entre el sud de la Costa Brava i el Garraf , llocs on no arribaran la tramuntana ni el mestral, els vents girin transitòriament a component marítim aportant humitat que es barrejarà amb l’aire fred en altura. Això comportarà la possibilitat de tempestes puntualment fortes i algun aiguat local, sobretot entre el Maresme i la Selva i especialment avançada la tarda, vespre i nit de dijous. Malgrat que la possibilitat és més elevada en aquestes comarques, el risc de tempesta intensa existirà també a Barcelona, al Baix Llobregat i, fins i tot, al Garraf. El Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya actualitza l’avís de situació meteorològica de perill (#avisosSMP) per vent Dj. 02:00 h a Dv. 02:00 h Possibilitat de ratxa màxima > 30 m/s (108 km/h) Grau de perill màxim 2/6 Hora local (h) = TU+2 https://t.co/5B9QEpdDRs — Meteocat (@meteocat) October 8, 2026 En aquest sentit, el Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya ha actualitzat els seus avisos per a dijous i els eleva en el cas de Barcelona a 3 sobre 6 a partir del migdia i fins a la mitjanit , davant la possibilitat de superar els 20 litres en mitja hora. Aquest darrer episodi es pot acabar entrada la nit amb una bona llampegada mar endins. També et pot interessar Els embassaments comencen la tardor al 75 %, la millor dada dels darrers sis anys Marcos Amores Sánchez 2 minuts de lectura Primeres jaquetes gruixudes aquest divendres La notícia serà també el posterior descens de la temperatura . Contundent sobretot si tenim en compte que venim de molt amunt i que anirem a parar, per uns dies, per sota del que seria habitual. Això implicarà una clatellada clara de la temperatura que ens durà mínimes de poc més de 12/13 ºC al centre, tant divendres com dissabte, i amb alguns valors que podrien baixar per primer cop per sota dels 10 ºC a la part més alta de Barcelona o al vessant vallesà de Collserola. Serà un primer tast de tardor que no tindrà continuïtat més endavant. La massa d’aire fred marxarà i el sol lluirà amb força durant el cap de setmana llarg , i això farà que la temperatura es recuperi aviat d’aquesta primera sotragada.

articles.body: (ACN) Antonio Carmona, l’ ex director de Rodalies a Catalunya, deixa Renfe i fitxa per Adif . La cara visible durant molts anys de l’operadora ferroviària a Catalunya s’incorporarà al gestor d’infraestructures com a coordinador de la xarxa de Rodalies , tal com indica el portal de contractació d’Adif. El càrrec inclourà funcions de responsable institucional i de comunicació. L’històric portaveu de Renfe va ser l’encarregat durant molts anys de comparèixer davant dels mitjans per donar explicacions en casos d’incidències o avaries al servei. A mitjans del 2024 va ser nomenat director de Rodalies de Catalunya càrrec del qual va ser rellevat a l’estiu del 2025. Actualment, el càrrec de direcció general de Rodalies l’ocupa Òscar Playà . articles.body: Vols saber què pots fer a Barcelona avui , demà o aquest mes? L’ Agenda de Barcelona et posa al dia de les propostes culturals. Et fem una llista d’ activitats i plans molts diversos , amb propostes, algunes de gratuïtes , per fer en família , el cap de setmana , a l’aire lliure , concerts , espectacles, exposicions i molt més! articles.body: L’Ajuntament de Barcelona ha adquirit més de 1.600 habitatges des del 2015 , segons ha explicat al Bon dia, Barcelona , el comissionat d’Habitatge, Joan Ramón Riera. També ha assegurat que l’Ajuntament no deixarà de fer aquestes adquisicions . De fet, ha apuntat que ja treballen en altres operacions a la ciutat. “Tenim un diàleg obert amb veïns a qui se’ls hi acaba el contracte, així com propietaris de finques”, ha explicat. També et pot interessar Barcelona crea un fons per comprar comerços “emblemàtics i estratègics” en risc de desaparèixer Ester Magdaleno Helena Molist Sancho 2 minuts de lectura Com es fan aquestes compres? L’Ajuntament disposa de diversos mecanismes per adquirir un habitatge. La més habitual és el tanteig i retracte , que permet a l’Administració pública adquirir de manera preferent un immoble. Una altra manera és a través de l’adjudicació d’habitatges protegits tant de nova promoció com recuperar-los. També pot comprar directament un habitatge a través dels fons d’emergència . També et pot interessar L’Ajuntament podrà cedir a entitats el dret a tanteig i retracte en la compra d’habitatge Marina Segura i Vidal 2 minuts de lectura Casa Orsola i Llenguadoc, 74, els casos més notoris Unes de les adquisicions que han tingut més rellevància mediàtica han estat els casos de la Casa Orsola i el l bloc de Llenguadoc, 74 , al barri de Sant Andreu de Palomar, perquè en tots dos casos hi vivien persones a punt de ser desnonades . Ara bé, l’Ajuntament els va adquirir per vies diferents. En el cas de la Casa Orsola , ho va fer a través del tanteig i retracte i va comprar la finca per 9,2 milions d’euros de manera conjunta amb Hàbitat3. En el cas de Llenguadoc, 74 , l’adquisició s’ha fet conjuntament amb la Generalitat a través del Fons d’Emergència Habitacional , dotat amb 25 milions d’euros. Riera ha apuntat que en els pròxims dies es coneixeran tots els detalls de l’operació. articles.body: 25 anys després de publicar el seu primer disc, Madee torna. Hem estat anys sense saber res del sextet català, que es distingeix per fer música indie rock amb un punt emo , però ara torna per publicar el seu vuitè disc d’estudi , titulat Bury me in the craters of the moon ( BCore ). “Voldríem que ens enterressin als cràters de la Lluna. Potser seríem els primers!”, han bromejat en una entrevista a La brama dos dels membres del grup, el guitarrista i vocalista Ramon Rodríguez i el baixista Pep Masiques , en referència al nom del disc. El dijous 22 d’octubre el presentaran a La Nau i ja tenen ganes que el seu públic en gaudeixi perquè “és un disc que té un so molt directe”, ha dit Masiques. Han avançat, però, que també tocaran els seus grans temes de sempre perquè el públic els demana. Un disc amb portada vintage La pintora Anna Gallés, qui va fer la imatge dels tres primers discos de la banda , és l’autora de la imatge d’aquest treball de Madee, que surt a la venda el 9 d’octubre. “Tornar a les imatges oníriques de l’Anna és com tornar a casa”, ha explicat Rodríguez. A més, dada curiosa, la pintura que va il·lustrar la portada del primer disc de Madee, Songs from Cydonia , és una obra que Rodríguez havia comprat en una exposició de Gallés un any abans de treure el primer disc de la banda, pensant que seria la portada del seu àlbum debut. I ho va ser. Madee Pel que fa a les lletres, totes són poemes de Mark Swanson , amb qui ja és el quart disc que fan. “És una experiència molt bonica, musicar els seus poemes”, han comentat els membres de Madee, en referència al fet que quan reben els poemes no saben com acabaran convertint-se en cançons. “L’energia és la mateixa, però potser ara som més conscients del que fem . Abans érem més impulsius”, ha explicat Rodríguez pel que fa al so. Tots dos han recordat que fa 36 anys que toquen plegats, des de l’adolescència, i en diferents formacions, tot i que Madee ha estat la més longeva. “El grup sempre ha estat una excusa per mantenir l’amistat amb vida “, han comentat. I també per desmitificar una mica el grup: som molt normals, no hi ha res de rock-and-roll . Som uns col·legues que fan discos”, ha explicat Rodríguez.

articles.body: L’Òscar Bautista, un infermer de 53 anys, ha volgut tota la vida treballar en emergències i sempre fora de l’hospital. La creació de la UIS el 2007 li va suposar una oportunitat per entrar-hi dos anys després i aplicar tots els coneixements en màsters en els pacients crítics i emergències que té. El Xavi Pla és company seu i ara també el seu cap. Té 37 anys i és un dels dos coordinadors de la unitat: s’encarrega de la distribució dels equips sobre el territori per atendre totes les sortides de màxima complexitat que apareguin: entrades en habitatges; manifestacions amb risc; entrades en locals d’oci; partits de Champions amb presència de seguidors violents; fuites biològiques, químiques o nuclears; atemptats, catàstrofes naturals o accidents amb múltiples afectats. Han presumit que treballen per parelles formades per un infermer i un tècnic d’Emergències Sanitàries, una unitat formada només per sanitaris, que responen al nom d’ORCA, l’indicatiu de l’emissora. articles.body: La Federació d’Entitats del Clot celebra mig segle de vida i ha decidit commemorar-ho amb una exposició col·laborativa . La mostra pretén explicar com ha canviat el barri i la seva gent a través dels records dels veïns. En aquest sentit, al taulell informatiu del Centre Cultural la Farinera del Clot hi han instal·lat una capsa per recollir fotografies, objectes, cartells i tot allò que representi algun moment dels 50 anys de la Federació d’Entitats del Clot. “Estem buscant records físics de qualsevol acte festiu que va organitzar la Federació després de la dictadura i així mostrar que la història de la Federació és la història del barri”, reivindica a l’ Infobarris Eva Concha, vocal de comunicació de la Federació. I afegeix que l’objectiu de la mostra és remarcar el paper de la Federació és acompanyar els veïns en la seva lluita i fomentar l’associacionisme . També et pot interessar Recuperar la memòria del Clot – Camp de l’Arpa a partir de fotografies i objectes quotidians Queralt Gómez Cuberes 2 minuts de lectura “Nosaltres proposem un oci autoorganitzat” Des de la Federació lamenten que la seva tasca és, tot i els 50 anys, encara força desconeguda i amb la mostra també volen aconseguir que més veïns coneguin el seu projecte. Josep Lluís Alonso, vocal de la Federació d’Entitats exposa que “la gent veu al carrer els gegants, els diables, els castellers i les colles de cultura popular, però no veuen totes les hores de coordinació i de diàleg que hi ha al darrere, que és el que som nosaltres”. A més, el nostre paper és el de promoure un oci autoorganitzat “que no depèn d’empresaris de la nit, ni d’indústries i que s’allunya del model comercial i s’apropa al veïnat “, afirma Alonso. Amb l’exposició també es vol posar en relleu aquesta faceta de la Federació. La crida per portar els records a la Farinera està oberta fins a finals d’any i de cara al 2027 es farà la inauguració oficial del recull final dels records del veïnat del Clot. També et pot interessar L’exposició “El Clot – Camp de l’Arpa desaparegut” Àlex Jassé Javier Arilla 1 minut de lectura
